overview: The Medford Historical Commission held a preferably preserved hearing for 110 Brooks Street, voted on the historic significance of Medford City Hall for a CPA grant application, and discussed initial planning for the city's upcoming 400th anniversary. The commission designated 110 Brooks Street as preferably preserved and confirmed City Hall's historic significance while reviewing updates on several local preservation initiatives.

items.title: 110 Brooks Street Preferably Preserved Hearing
items.summary: Following public and homeowner comments, the commission voted that 110 Brooks Street is preferably preserved, referring proposed plans to a subcommittee to review architectural details during the demolition delay.

items.title: City Hall CPA Project Determination of Significance
items.summary: The commission voted that City Hall is historically significant for a CPA funding application for bathroom accessibility upgrades, recommending that the CPC condition funding on completing a comprehensive building assessment.

items.title: Medford Quadricennial Celebration Planning
items.summary: Community Preservation Act Manager Theresa Dupont presented early concepts for forming a committee to coordinate programming and budgeting for Medford's upcoming 400th anniversary in 2030.

items.title: Properties Under Demolition Delay and Inventory Updates
items.summary: Commissioners reviewed updates on 56 Wareham Street plans and discussed monitoring 161 Main Street without ordering a Form B survey at this time.

items.title: Building Permit Review Subcommittee Update
items.summary: Chair Keenan reported on an upcoming meeting with the building department to coordinate permit reviews and clarify submittal requirements for historic properties.

items.title: Cross Street Cemetery Archaeological Project
items.summary: The commission received an update regarding the PAL contracting status and timeline for state archaeological permitting at the former Cross Street Cemetery parcel.

items.title: Thomas Brooks Park Phase 2 Update
items.summary: The commission announced a public Zoom meeting for October 22, 2024, to present Phase 2 master plan updates and archaeological capping options for Thomas Brooks Park.

items.title: Survey Projects and Grant Applications
items.summary: The commission discussed submitting a grant application to survey historical properties in West Medford's Hastings Heights neighborhood.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: The commission approved the meeting minutes from September 2024.
